item.title: - Who ages, who does not age? What is called the wrong path? What is an obstacle to the Dhamma? What destroys day and night?…
item.description:
- Who ages, who does not age?
What is called the wrong path?
What is an obstacle to the Dhamma?
What destroys day and night?
What defiles the holy life?
What is a bath without water?
How many openings in the world
Upon which the mind does not dwell?
I have come to ask the Blessed One —
Please tell me the answers!
- Form in beings ages,
The name-nature does not age,
Greed is called the wrong path,
Craving is an obstacle to the Dhamma.
Aging destroys day and night,
Women defile the holy life —
Ensnared in this defilement
Are all beings.
Austerities and the holy life
Are a bath without water.
There are six openings in the world
Upon which the mind does not dwell:
Laziness and heedlessness,
Lethargy and lack of self-control,
Drowsiness and sloth —
These six openings should be
Completely abandoned.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.76

item.title: “Monks, those ascetics or brahmins in the past … in the future … in the present who regard whatever in the world is agreeable and…
item.description:
“Monks, those ascetics or brahmins in the past … in the future … in the present who regard whatever in the world is agreeable and enticing as permanent, as happiness, as healthy, as safe, as self — they increase craving. Those who increase craving, increase attachment. Those who increase attachment, increase suffering. Those who increase suffering are not freed from birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. I say that they are not freed from suffering.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 12.66

item.title: “Monks, I do not see any other fetter by which beings, fettered, wander and transmigrate for a long time as this fetter of craving. Monks,…
item.description:
“Monks, I do not see any other fetter by which beings, fettered, wander and transmigrate for a long time as this fetter of craving. Monks, fettered by the fetter of craving, beings wander and transmigrate for a long time.

One with craving as companion
Wanders on for a long time.
Neither here nor there beyond such becoming
Can they cross the wandering.

Knowing this peril — that craving
Is the origin of suffering —
Free from craving, without clinging,
Mindful, the monk lives the homeless life.”

From: Itivuttaka 15

item.title: Like a newly decorated medicine box, This foul body is adorned for the occasion — Enough to fool a fool, But not one who seeks…
item.description:
Like a newly decorated medicine box,
This foul body is adorned for the occasion —
Enough to fool a fool,
But not one who seeks the far shore.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 82 – Raṭṭhapālasutta

item.title: “Monks, there are these three ways that sensual desire arises. What three? Sensual desire for present objects, delight in one’s own creations, and acceptance of…
item.description:
“Monks, there are these three ways that sensual desire arises. What three? Sensual desire for present objects, delight in one’s own creations, and acceptance of what is created by others. These, monks, are the three ways that sensual desire arises.

The gods who enjoy sense pleasures,
The gods of great power,
The gods who delight in creation,
And the gods who wield power over others —
Enjoying sense pleasures,
Here and there in various existences,
They do not go beyond the wandering.

Knowing this peril,
The wise should abandon all sensual desires,
Whether divine or human,
Here and in future states.

Those who have cut the stream
So hard to cross,
Who have broken the bond
To what is dear and beautiful,
Having made an end of suffering,
Without remainder,
Those noble ones who have seen,
The wise with knowledge,
Having rightly known the destruction of birth,
Do not go to renewed existence.”

From: Itivuttaka 95

item.title: “And, Carpenter, how do these unwholesome thoughts arise? Their arising has also been taught. It should be said that they arise from perception. What is…
item.description:
“And, Carpenter, how do these unwholesome thoughts arise? Their arising has also been taught. It should be said that they arise from perception. What is perception? There are various perceptions, many and diverse: sensual perception, ill-will perception, harmfulness perception. From these, unwholesome thoughts arise.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 78 – Samaṇamuṇḍikasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, I do not see any other class of things that is as diverse as the mind. Those beings in the animal realm — such…
item.description:
“Monks, I do not see any other class of things that is as diverse as the mind. Those beings in the animal realm — such beings are diverse because of their minds. Therefore, monks, one should constantly reflect on one’s own mind thus: ‘For a long time, this mind has been defiled by greed, hatred, and delusion. Through the defilement of the mind, beings are defiled. Through the purification of the mind, beings are purified.’”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.100
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, there are these three kinds of craving. What three? Craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, craving for non-existence. These, monks, are the three…
item.description:
“Monks, there are these three kinds of craving. What three? Craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, craving for non-existence. These, monks, are the three kinds of craving.

Bound by the bondage of craving,
Their minds attached to becoming and non-becoming,
Bound by Māra’s bondage,
Those beings are not secure from bondage.
They go on in the wandering,
Gone to birth and death.

But those who have abandoned craving,
Free from craving for becoming and non-becoming,
Having reached the far shore,
In this very world, they have attained
The destruction of the defilements.”

From: Itivuttaka 58

item.title: “One who clings, monk, is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One.” - “I understand, Blessed One! I…
item.description:
“One who clings, monk, is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One.” - “I understand, Blessed One! I understand, Well-gone One!” - “How, monk, do you understand in detail the meaning of my brief statement?” - “One who clings to form, venerable sir, is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One. One who clings to feeling … to perception … to formations … to consciousness is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One. Venerable sir, I understand in detail the meaning of the Blessed One’s brief statement thus.” - “Good, good, monk! Good, monk! Thus you understand in detail the meaning of my brief statement. One who clings to form, monk, is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One. One who clings to feeling … to perception … to formations … to consciousness is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.63

item.title: “Monks, how is a monk a samana (ascetic)? He has quieted down evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing painful…
item.description:
“Monks, how is a monk a samana (ascetic)? He has quieted down evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing painful results, leading to future birth, aging, and death. Thus, monks, a monk is a samana.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 39 – Mahāhatthipadopamasutta
